channel.title: The Brussels Times
channel.description: Latest Brussels posts from The Brussels Times.

item.title: Trade Unions refuse Bouchez's request to postpone protests
More than 13 kilograms of cannabis found during search in Jette
item.description: Police in Jette seized 13.53kg of cannabis, seven bottles of GHB and €8,670 in cash during a search of a flat on Tuesday, arresting two suspects.

item.title: More than a quarter of schools in Brussels overexposed to NO₂
item.description: "It is unacceptable that, in Brussels, going to school still means being exposed to toxic fumes."

item.title: The Brussels Times Gig Guide: What are the best concerts this October?
item.description: Check out this month's unmissable gigs in the Belgian capital for your and your friends to enjoy.

item.title: Fake cannabis shops in Brussels linked to Telegram drug dealers
item.description: An undercover conversation by The Brussels Times and one of these 'businesses' uncovered the scale of these operations.

item.title: Ixelles commune introduces free parking permits for garages blocked by roadworks
item.description: The new permits will apply when roadworks affect a parking space for at least 10 working days.

item.title: Brussels Airport to cancel 140 flights due to ground handler action
item.description: Around 140 flights landing and departing at Brussels Airport on Friday will be cancelled, as ground handler Alyzia is severely affected by the national actions.

item.title: Over 100,000 people now looking for work in Brussels
item.description: More than 100,000 people are now registered as jobseekers in Brussels for the first time since 2016.

item.title: Brussels among European cities most dependent on fossil fuels for heating
item.description: Brussels ranks among the European capitals most dependent on fossil fuels to heat buildings, prompting Greenpeace to call for a clear deadline to phase out gas.

item.title: 'Not just a blip': Brussels homes are taking longer to sell
item.description: Houses and apartments in the Belgian capital are spending more time on the market, and sellers are cutting prices more often.

item.title: New rail safety programme aims to protect visually impaired young people in Belgium
item.description: Belgian rail infrastructure manager Infrabel has launched a new programme to teach visually impaired young people how to stay safe around railway tracks.

item.title: Man seriously injured after his leg got stuck at Botanique metro station
item.description: Medical professionals found the man with his leg stuck in a shutter leading to the metro station.

item.title: Budget negotiations in Brussels paused, but will resume on Sunday
item.description: The talks proved difficult, with one of the main sticking points being fares at Brussels public transport operator STIB.

item.title: Over 100 Brussels and Walloon businesses open doors to public this Sunday
item.description: Craftspeople, shops, SMEs, family businesses, industrial firms and innovation companies will welcome visitors.

item.title: Designing around what already exists instead of building anew: Brussels' circular architecture
item.description: “Something that was built 100 years ago can last for another 100 years.”

item.title: Brussels gets its first whisky, made by two expats in Koekelberg
item.description: After three years of ageing, Tipsy Tribe has released what it describes as the first whisky made in Brussels.

item.title: ‘The penis is not aggressive’: The artist who shocked Brussels with his murals
item.description: For the first time, Bonom seems ready to reveal the workings of his inner mind that led to creations of Brussels' most polarising murals.

item.title: Brussels Airport luggage handlers arrested in drug network bust
item.description: 21 people have been detained over cocaine and weed trafficking network that allegedly recruited baggage handlers at Brussels Airport to take out drugs from bags before they arrived.

item.title: What to do in Brussels this weekend: 2 – 4 October
item.description: From a rave based on a fan-favourite kids movie to a self-guided adventure to defeat a Vampire King, start October right with The Brussels Times' weekend picks.

item.title: Father sentenced to life in prison for killing his autistic toddler
item.description: Mohammed Taoussi has been found guilty of murdering his three-year-old son Wassim, with the jury retaining a discriminatory motive linked to the child's suspected autism.
